data.title: Sneaky 2FA Impossible Device Shift — User-Agent Mismatch per Auth Step
data.description: Detects the "impossible device shift" signature characteristic of Sneaky 2FA and related AiTM phishing kits. Sneaky 2FA uses different hardcoded User-Agent strings per authentication step — Safari on iOS for the Login:login step and Edge on Windows for the Login:resume step. This pattern is detectable via correlation of mismatched User-Agents within the same correlation ID within 10 minutes. This detection also catches Dadsec (missing User-Agent), Tycoon 2FA (rare User-Agent values), and W3LL OV6 (inconsistent UAs).

detection.condition: count(distinct UserAgent) by CorrelationId >= 2 AND timeframe < 10 minutes

queries.cql:
// CrowdStrike CQL for Sneaky 2FA Impossible Device Shift Detection
// Correlates mismatched User-Agents within same authentication flow
#repo="azure_signinlogs"
ResultType="0"
| groupBy([CorrelationId, UserPrincipalName], function=[count(field=UserAgent, distinct=true, as=UACount), collect([UserAgent], as=UserAgents), collect([IPAddress], as=IPs), min(@timestamp, as=MinTime), max(@timestamp, as=MaxTime)], span=10m)
| UACount >= 2
// High confidence: Safari/iOS + Edge/Windows combination (Sneaky 2FA signature)
| UserAgents=/Safari/ AND UserAgents=/Edge/
    OR UserAgents=/iPhone/ AND UserAgents=/Windows/
| select([UserPrincipalName, CorrelationId, UACount, UserAgents,
          IPs, MinTime, MaxTime])
| sort(UACount, order=desc)
queries.kql:
// KQL: Sneaky 2FA Impossible Device Shift Detection
// Correlates mismatched User-Agents within same authentication flow
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where ResultType == 0
| summarize
    UACount = dcount(UserAgent),
    UserAgents = make_set(UserAgent),
    IPs = make_set(IPAddress),
    MinTime = min(TimeGenerated),
    MaxTime = max(TimeGenerated)
  by CorrelationId, UserPrincipalName
| where UACount >= 2
| where datetime_diff('minute', MaxTime, MinTime) <= 10
// Convert dynamic array to string for substring matching
| extend UA_str = tostring(UserAgents)
// High confidence: Safari/iOS + Edge/Windows combination (Sneaky 2FA signature)
| where (UA_str has "Safari" and UA_str has "Edge")
    or (UA_str has "iPhone" and UA_str has "Windows")
| project UserPrincipalName, CorrelationId, UACount, UserAgents,
          IPs, MinTime, MaxTime
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Sneaky 2FA Impossible Device Shift")`
`comment("Detects User-Agent mismatch within same auth correlation ID")`
index=azure sourcetype=azure:aad:signin ResultType=0
| stats dc(UserAgent) AS ua_count,
        values(UserAgent) AS user_agents,
        values(IPAddress) AS ips,
        min(_time) AS first_event,
        max(_time) AS last_event
  BY CorrelationId, UserPrincipalName
| where ua_count >= 2
| eval window_minutes = round((last_event - first_event) / 60, 1)
| where window_minutes <= 10
| search (user_agents="*Safari*" AND user_agents="*Edge*")
    OR (user_agents="*iPhone*" AND user_agents="*Windows*")
| sort - ua_count

references: Phishing kits and AiTM platforms: a comprehensive threat intelligence reference (2026)
falsepositives: Extremely rare in legitimate authentication — different User-Agents within the same correlation ID should not occur in normal browser authentication
